change.author: Udit Takkar

findings.title: retryCount delete branch is not limited to SMS reminders
findings.body: The first OR branch has `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, but the new `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch has no method filter. `retryCount` is a column on every `WorkflowReminder` row. This SMS-only cron therefore deletes any reminder with `retryCount > 1`, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows. Only this handler writes `retryCount` today (no other `retryCount` match under packages/ touches it), so it is latent now. The first time another reminder type uses the column, this cron will silently delete its rows. Fix: `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

findings.title: Update inside catch can throw and abort the whole batch
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block is not guarded. If the DB call fails, for example during the same outage that caused the original error, the exception escapes the `for` loop. Every remaining reminder is skipped and the handler returns a 500. The same applies to the `else` update at line 179, which sits inside the `try` and falls into the catch. Wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch, or extract a small `incrementRetryCount(id, current)` helper. The helper would also remove the duplicated update at lines 179-186 and 190-197.

findings.title: Reminders are dropped silently after 2 failures, and the increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: `gt: 1` deletes a row once `retryCount` reaches 2. A reminder therefore gets only two attempts, and the deletion is not logged. `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` when the user or team is SMS-locked (twilioProvider.ts:92-95) and throws on a rate limit. Both now count as failures, so a temporary lock or rate limit permanently removes the reminder, and no one is told. Please confirm that two attempts is intended, and consider logging the deletion. Also, `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is computed from a value read earlier in the run. Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` is atomic and avoids lost updates if two cron runs overlap.

findings.title: No tests for the retry and deletion behaviour
findings.body: The change adds new behaviour: retryCount increments on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result and on a thrown error, and rows are deleted once retryCount exceeds 1. No test covers any of it. At minimum, add a test for the delete filter and one for the increment on failure.

contracts.action: Cron deleteMany now also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1
contracts.equivalent_path: The same deleteMany, whose original filter was method SMS and scheduledDate <= now
contracts.before_after: Before, only SMS rows past their scheduled date were deleted. Now an OR adds a branch that matches any method with retryCount > 1.
contracts.visible_effect: A failing SMS reminder is deleted after 2 failed attempts, so the recipient never receives it. Nothing is shown to the user.
contracts.failure_mode: The missing method filter means non-SMS rows with retryCount > 1 would also be deleted. Today only this handler writes retryCount.

contracts.action: Increment retryCount when scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws
contracts.equivalent_path: The success branch at lines 168-177 updates scheduled and referenceId for the same row
contracts.before_after: Before, failures were retried on every cron run indefinitely. Now each failure increments a stored counter, and the row is deleted on the next run once the counter exceeds 1.
contracts.visible_effect: Reminders stop being retried and are removed after 2 failures. This includes temporary SMS-lock results, where scheduleSMS returns undefined (twilioProvider.ts:92-95).
contracts.failure_mode: The update in the catch is unguarded. If it throws, the loop aborts and the request returns 500. The bound on the whole operation is the 2-failure limit per row. A single run makes at most one attempt per row, with no internal loop or timeout, so the per-run cost is unchanged.

summary: The change adds a retry counter that deletes SMS reminders after 2 failed scheduling attempts. One bug: the new delete branch has no `method: SMS` filter, so it would also delete non-SMS reminders. Smaller concerns: the unguarded update in the catch block, the non-atomic increment, deletion with no log, and no tests. The migration and schema change are fine.
